purpose: Fifty new invented examples for editorial stress-testing of a generic dossier definition. Not real news, corpus research, a Luna benchmark, or external gold labels.
definition_under_review: A dossier collects reports whose main subject is the same specific reported occurrence or explicitly bounded continuing episode. Its identity is defined by the action or occurrence, participants or affected object, and compatible time, place and distinguishing evidence. Claims, corrections and uncertainty remain attributed to their sources.
rules_under_review: Record event kind, core action, scope and distinguishing anchors. A continuing episode needs evidence of continuity; time elapsed, expanded area or common cause alone cannot settle identity. A documented end followed by a distinct initiation supports a new event. Unclear recovery/restart stays uncertain.

New casualty counts, perspectives or reporting dates can update the same event. Contradictory occurrence identifiers require review. A correction can change identity or disprove an alleged occurrence; preserve claims and version lineage.

A disclosure, filing, decision or other new action can have its own linked dossier when it is the article's main event. Merely publishing new information about an existing event does not create a new event. One announcement about several occurrences does not make those occurrences one event.

Read headline, lead and body together to establish one focal event. Background references are allowed. Two independent occurrences with coequal focus mean multiple_focal_events; do not assign the whole article to one dossier.

Require positive identity evidence: an occurrence-specific reference or a sufficiently distinctive combination of action, affected object and context. No fixed number of generic matching fields suffices. Unknown time/place does not prove difference; missing facts are not wildcard agreements. Otherwise uncertain.

Shared cause, organization, legal case or topic can support a related-event link without membership. A filing and a judgment differ even with the same case ID. Domain relevance is a separate corpus-selection policy.
review_instructions: Review exactly these descriptions without external facts. For each item give eligibility_a and eligibility_b from clear_single_event, multiple_focal_events, not_event_focused, insufficient_information. Give relation from same_event, related_but_different_event, different_event, uncertain only if both are clear_single_event; otherwise relation=null. Flag policy_gap=true when the wording leaves a relevant boundary open, even if you can choose a reasonable label. Explain in one short sentence. This is conceptual definition review, not measured real-world performance.

cases.a: A report describes ferry Aurora striking pier 4 at Lark Harbour at 08:10 on 6 May. Its main account is the passengers' evacuation.
cases.b: A Spanish report describes the 6 May Aurora collision at Lark Harbour pier 4, concentrating on the harbour authority's response during the collision. It identifies the same 08:10 occurrence.

cases.a: Flight CR218 made one emergency return to Cedar Airport at 23:40 local time on 7 July. This report centers on that landing.
cases.b: The report identifies the CR218 emergency return as occurring at 01:40 UTC on 8 July and explicitly states that this is the same landing at 23:40 local time on 7 July.

cases.a: Article A reports tram collision T18, provisionally locating it outside Hill Street station.
cases.b: Article B describes collision T18 and corrects the location to the adjacent depot entrance, explaining that the initial report used the station as a landmark. It reports no second collision.

cases.a: A report on stadium stairway collapse S4 says eight people were injured.
cases.b: A later report updates the injury count for collapse S4 to eleven. The article remains centered on the collapse and does not report a new accident.

cases.a: A report says demolition of Old Mill chimney occurred on Friday and identifies online clip V7 as evidence.
cases.b: A correction explicitly addresses that report: V7 shows the chimney's demolition last year, and no demolition happened on Friday. Its focus is correcting the alleged Friday occurrence, not a new investigation or official sanction.

cases.a: The national recall notice R24 withdraws all lot L8 baby seats following one issued safety order. The article centers on that recall.
cases.b: A regional report explains how the same notice R24 affects local shops carrying lot L8. It reports the original recall, not a separate local order.

cases.a: The manufacturer issued recall R25 for baby-seat lot L8 in March.
cases.b: In June it issued recall R26 for lot L9, explicitly calling this a separate recall from R25. Both reports center on their respective recall orders.

cases.a: A report forecasts the landfall of named cyclone Mira, storm identifier M26, and describes that anticipated landfall as its main event.
cases.b: A later report describes the actual landfall of cyclone M26, with its recorded place and time. It explicitly identifies this as the landfall forecast in A.

cases.a: An article previews the scheduled opening performance of the Elm Festival, booking E26, focusing on that performance rather than an announcement ceremony.
cases.b: A review reports the completed opening performance E26, describing the same scheduled participants and programme.

cases.a: A preview describes concert booking C91 at West Hall on 9 June.
cases.b: An update says booking C91 is moved to East Hall on 16 June; original tickets remain valid. It explicitly describes one postponed performance, not an additional booking.

cases.a: Concert C91 was canceled and refunded. The article focuses on C91 and its canceled status.
cases.b: The artists later schedule concert C98 with a new programme and separate tickets, explicitly describing it as a new event following cancellation of C91.

cases.a: A contemporaneous account describes the 2008 collapse of the North Viaduct.
cases.b: A retrospective reconstructs only that same 2008 collapse using newly available witness accounts. It reports no anniversary ceremony, new inquiry or other focal action.

cases.a: A report describes the 2025 opening procession of the annual Reed Fair.
cases.b: A report describes the 2026 opening procession of Reed Fair and explicitly distinguishes it from last year's procession.

cases.a: A sports report covers the March league fixture K17 between East Club and West Club.
cases.b: A second report covers their September cup fixture K88. The teams and venue are the same but both fixture identifiers and competitions differ.

cases.a: Workers begin strike action ST4, announced as one continuous action from Monday through the following Friday, including the intervening weekend.
cases.b: A later report describes the continuing ST4 stoppage on its eighth day. It expressly states that the strike was not ended during the weekend when the workplace was normally closed.

cases.a: Strike ST4 ended after a signed settlement and a documented return to work.
cases.b: A month later the same workers begin ST9 over a new pay dispute. The report explicitly describes a new strike after ST4 ended.

cases.a: A ticket network stops working on Monday because of fault F8. The report says some services briefly returned on Tuesday but it is unclear whether the disruption ended.
cases.b: A Wednesday report describes ticket failures involving F8, without establishing whether this is uninterrupted disruption or a fresh outage after recovery.

cases.a: A water-main rupture causes outage W12 across Brook Ward. The report describes the initial disruption.
cases.b: An update describes continued W12 disruption and the evolving affected area. It confirms that service has not yet been restored and remains focused on the outage, not a separately reported repair contract or ceremony.

cases.a: Storm N7 causes the bridge at East Ford to collapse at 10:00; this report centers on that collapse.
cases.b: The same storm causes a different bridge at West Ford to collapse at 15:00; this report centers on the second collapse. Both collapses are independently identified.

cases.a: A report centers on the continuing Delta flood episode, describing its regional extent and duration.
cases.b: A report centers on a separately identified boat rescue R8 undertaken during the Delta flood. The rescue has its own start, participants and completion; the flood is background.

cases.a: A report describes an explosion at Foundry 6 followed immediately by flames in the same structure, treating them as one uninterrupted industrial accident.
cases.b: Another account calls that same uninterrupted Foundry 6 accident a fire, explains its initial explosion and centers on the ongoing burning. It reports no separate ignition or intervening end.

cases.a: A report describes the first warehouse fire at Dock Road; officials have not yet decided whether the neighbouring warehouse was part of the same fire.
cases.b: A report describes flames at the neighbouring warehouse and says they may have spread from the first site or begun independently. No source settles whether there was one continuous fire or two.

cases.a: An article reports the theft of painting P4 from the Valley Museum.
cases.b: Another article centers on police formally opening investigation I3 into that theft; details of the theft serve as background to the new investigative action.

cases.a: An article reports the filing of case L55 about a disputed property sale.
cases.b: An article reports the judgment issued in case L55 nine months later. Each is centered on its named procedural action.

cases.a: An article reports the first-instance judgment in case L55.
cases.b: Another article reports the filing of an appeal against that judgment. It is primarily about the appeal filing.

cases.a: A report describes order J33 issued by the Harbor Court on 4 April.
cases.b: An analysis in another language explains the reasoning of that same J33 order. It is centered on the order and reports no later ruling or appeal.

cases.a: A report centers on the public announcement of a proposed merger between Oak and Pine, transaction M8.
cases.b: A report centers on the legal closing of M8 six months later, expressly distinguishing closing from the earlier announcement.

cases.a: The first shipment D1 under supply contract C4 was delivered to the port on Monday; the article centers on this delivery.
cases.b: The second shipment D2 under C4 was delivered on Friday; the article centers on this separately tracked delivery, not the contract as a whole.

cases.a: A report covers the launch event L10 for the Sable bicycle.
cases.b: An essay discusses bicycle frame materials in general, using Sable and four older models as examples. It has no focal launch or other particular occurrence.

cases.a: An article examines long-term commuting preferences using statistics from many years. It is not centered on the release of any one report.
cases.b: Another essay argues for better cycle lanes using examples from several cities and decades, with no focal occurrence.

cases.a: An article centers on regulator briefing B6 announcing findings about three unrelated factory accidents on different dates. The briefing is the main new action.
cases.b: An article reconstructs the accident at Factory Two, one of those three accidents, concentrating on the physical occurrence rather than briefing B6.

cases.a: A report centers on briefing B6 and describes its announcement of findings about three factory accidents as background content of the briefing.
cases.b: Another report centers on the same B6 briefing, emphasizing reactions in the room and the publication of its findings. No separate briefing is described.

cases.a: A report gives equal, sustained attention to two independently identified bus crashes in different towns, with no dominant crash.
cases.b: A report focuses solely on the first of those crashes.

cases.a: A roundup gives ten unrelated weddings separate sections of comparable prominence, with no main wedding.
cases.b: An article focuses on one wedding appearing in the roundup.

cases.a: A company history follows Cedar Works from its founding through several acquisitions, strikes and closures; no event dominates.
cases.b: A report focuses on Cedar Works' independently identified 2012 acquisition of Moss Ltd.

cases.a: A report describes a fatal crash at Rose Junction on 8 August, identified as RC8.
cases.b: An opinion article argues for a national transport policy, mentioning RC8 briefly among other examples. The policy argument, rather than any one crash, is its organizing subject.

cases.a: A report describes climbing accident A7 involving Lina Vale.
cases.b: A profile surveys Lina Vale's childhood, training, achievements and family. A7 is one background episode and no single occurrence organizes the profile.

cases.a: An initial report describes the collapse of Footbridge F2 on 2 February.
cases.b: An explanatory article reconstructs why F2 collapsed that day, with the same structure and witnesses. It reports no new inquiry, ruling or other focal action.

cases.a: A report says the Grove Festival edition G26 was canceled; it focuses on that edition and its alleged canceled status.
cases.b: A correction disputes the cancellation and documents that G26 proceeded. It remains centered on the status of that same festival edition, not a new corrective ceremony or action.

cases.a: A short report mentions an equipment accident at Norfield Foods, without specifying the factory, date, device or any unique occurrence reference.
cases.b: Another short report mentions an equipment accident at Norfield Foods with similarly missing identifying details. Neither says it refers to the other's occurrence.

cases.a: An article describes an interim injunction in case P90 on 1 March.
cases.b: An article describes a later final judgment in the same P90 case on 1 November. Each explicitly concerns its own court action.

cases.a: An undated article describes the Elm Expo opening but omits its edition, location and participants.
cases.b: Another undated article describes an Elm Expo opening. The expo occurs annually in different towns, and neither article identifies which edition it covers.

cases.a: A report identifies the towing of vessel Bright Star, registry VS10, after breakdown on voyage V41. It focuses on the tow's crew.
cases.b: A passenger account identifies VS10, voyage V41 and the same tow, without stating its date. Its focus is passengers' experience of that operation.

cases.a: A report describes the auction sale of painting The Green Stair, lot AU62, at auction session AS9.
cases.b: An undated report identifies the same AS9 lot AU62 sale and the same buyer, but uses an alternative translated title for the painting.

cases.a: A report describes an accident at noon involving lift unit EL4 in Tower Lane, with no incident reference.
cases.b: A report describes an accident at noon in Tower Lane but names lift unit EL9. It is unclear whether there were two accidents or an identifier error; no correction or explicit separation is available.

cases.a: A report describes an identified volcanic eruption on a remote island.
cases.b: A report describes an unrelated chess championship final in another country. No shared occurrence or concrete causal relationship is reported.

cases.a: A dossier summary says only that a goods train of Rail North derailed near Elm in spring. It omits the train number and exact date even though the source collection contains those details.
cases.b: An article identifies a Rail North derailment near Elm in spring, train RN14. Several derailments occurred there that season; the supplied summary does not establish which it represents.

cases.a: A dossier summary explicitly records unresolved disagreement between its sources over whether a report describes the June or September session of the Harbor Council; it does not select one.
cases.b: An article focuses on a vote at the September session. The supplied summary cannot establish whether its focal vote was at that session or the June session.

cases.a: An article centers on a city decision to close Pool South, announced during press conference PC3.
cases.b: An article centers on a separate city decision to fund Library North, announced during the same PC3. Both describe their respective decisions, not PC3 as the focal event.

cases.a: A report describes the jointly signed river-cleanup agreement AG8 between North Town and South Town, emphasizing North Town's signatories.
cases.b: A report describes the same AG8 signing, emphasizing South Town's signatories and using different translated place names. It explicitly identifies the same jointly signed instrument and ceremony.
